intro: We can find heights and distances that are hard to measure directly, such as the height of a tower, using angles and trigonometric ratios. Always draw a figure with the right angle and mark the known side and angle first.
keyPoints: Angle of elevation: the angle between the horizontal and the line of sight when looking UP at an object.
Angle of depression: the angle between the horizontal and the line of sight when looking DOWN.
Use tan when height and base are involved, sin or cos when the slant length (hypotenuse) is involved.

examples.title: Height of a tower
examples.problem: From a point 30 m away from the foot of a tower, the angle of elevation of its top is 30°. Find the height of the tower.

examples.title: Length of a kite string
examples.problem: A kite is flying at a height of 60 m. Its string makes an angle of 60° with the ground. Find the length of the string (assume no slack).

examples.title: Rope and pole
examples.problem: A circus artist climbs a 20 m long rope tied from the top of a vertical pole to the ground. The rope makes 30° with the ground. Find the height of the pole.

practice.question: The angle of elevation of the top of a tower from a point 100 m from its foot is 45°. Find its height.
A ladder makes an angle of 60° with the ground and its foot is 2.5 m from the wall. Find the length of the ladder.
The shadow of a pole is equal to its height. What is the sun's altitude?
